summary: Contestants will demonstrate their knowledge of medical billing and health insurance concepts and procedures. The event includes an objective and application assessment covering topics such as claim forms, insurance types, and billing terminology. Both secondary and postsecondary students may participate individually.
time_limits: no more than ten (10) minutes orientation
no more than sixty (60) minutes testing time
no more than ten (10) minutes wrap-up
what_to_bring: Published and/or unpublished non -electronic written reference materials
(Optional) Cordless calculator: Electronic devices will be monitored according to ACT standards. See NLC Calculator Guidelines. Contestants who violate this rule will be disqualified.
competencies: Demonstrate knowledge of full revenue -cycle workflow, including payment reconciliation, collections, and patient account management
Demonstrate understanding of various types of health insurance
Demonstrate the ability to complete health insurance claim forms and to audit submitted claims for accuracy, compliance, and completeness
Demonstrate the ability to verify insurance eligibility and benefits and to prepare and submit prior authorization requests
Identify, define, and correctly use health insurance and medical billing terminology essential to eligibility verification, claims processing, and reimbursement procedures
judging_notes: AI Policy Level 1 No AI Allowed
No equipment, supplies, or materials other than those specified for an event will be allowed in the testing area
No previous Business Professionals of America tests (handwritten, photocopied, or keyed) may be taken into the testing area. Violation of this rule will result in disqualification.
eligibility_notes: Any secondary or postsecondary division contestant may enter this application event.
